findings.summary: Critic protocol step 7 could not be performed against recording 368a3b30. Its upload status and Replay query results rest solely on builder-authored artifacts (.replay/browser-session.json, evidence/browser-proof.json, evidence/replay-interrogation.json, evidence/gate-summary.json). evidence/replay-interrogation.json is produced by no committed script and is structurally the same class of unreproducible hand-authored artifact that critic 2 flagged in its Finding 1.
mitigatingFacts: The substantive AC7 fact — zero console errors — is now backed by a committed executable assertion: scripts/e0-t01-replay-flow.js:157-168 throws on any console error, console warning, request failure, or page response >= 400.

Critic 2's console-count confound is genuinely removed: the deliberate edit failure is now an HTTP-200 application error (scripts/e0-t01-replay-flow.js:88-94), so no browser resource-load error is emitted.

The counting definition is now explicitly disclosed in evidence/browser-proof.json:71-79 (flowConsoleErrors, playwrightCliConsoleErrors, replayConsoleErrors) and evidence/browser-proof.json:107-111 (pageResponses.observedStatuses with a redirect note).
The same-session MP4 is byte-authenticated by this critic.
This gap is caused by the critic session's environment, not by any deficiency the builder can remedy through rework.

findings.summary: readme.md:381 states that `scripts/e0-t01-replay-metadata.json` "makes its lifecycle recording queryable by Replay", and evidence/browser-proof.json:6 cites it as metadataFile. The committed file contains exactly `{}` — an empty object supplying no title, no test metadata, and nothing that would make a recording queryable. The stated purpose of a committed evidence artifact is not true of its contents.

Two committed artifacts describing the same session disagree, and one zero-count is structurally unable to observe the error it implies. evidence/replay-interrogation.json:30-32 reports statusDistribution {"2xx": 21} for all 21 requests, while evidence/browser-proof.json:109 reports observedStatuses [200, 201, 302] — a 302 is not 2xx. Separately, the deliberate identity-spoof probe is issued through Playwright's APIRequestContext (scripts/e0-t01-replay-flow.js:143-146), not through the page, so its 403 appears in neither page-level response capture nor Replay's network panel; consistently, replay-interrogation.json records only 2 PATCH requests and no 4xx. The reported "0 failed requests" is therefore not evidence that error paths were exercised, and that boundary is not disclosed the way the console-counting boundary now is.
